subject: Trying to break Stan's limitations on not using parameters for time in the ODE solver?

messages.author: 4b681bcd9d4d425d
messages.subject: Trying to break Stan's limitations on not using parameters for time in the ODE solver?
parts:
Hi all,

This may be tilting at windmills, but I'm trying to figure out if there is a way to have an uncertain start time for my ODE; if I'm unsure when an epidemic starts, I'd like to be able to model that, and find the best fit for a dataset for the start time, as well as other parameters. (I didn't see anything about this in the forum history.)

In Stan, the t0 and t inputs into integrate_ODE are fixed; is there any clever way to get around this? (If so, how bad an idea is it to do?)

The obvious idea is to have the start values be smaller, but I think there is an effective lower bound on how few infections I can start with. (That is, 1e-25 doesn't make the sampler happy, and specifying a prior on it is kind of nasty.) Also, this doesn't capture the dynamics well; it ramps up over time, instead of starting above 1 when the infection is imported/emerges.

Thanks for any help, or potential workarounds,
David

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Trying to break Stan's limitations on not using parameters for time in the ODE solver?
parts:
I don't know what you are suggesting, exactly.

The differential equation system does not use t; I would need to change the offset outside of the ODE system solver. If I offset by a non-multiple of the values to solve at, I need to either adjust the times at which to solve, or use some rough linear kludge, or slow method, to infer the values at the locations I actually need.

As a simple example, how would I do this with Michael Betancourt's compartmental SIR+B model, attached - let's say I know that the bacteria in the y0 were introduced at some point, but I don't know when.

Cheers,
David

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Trying to break Stan's limitations on not using parameters for time in the ODE solver?
parts:
1. Declare a parameter for the initial time.

2. Pass that parameter to ode_integrate

3. Pass initial time t0 = 0 to ode_integrate.

4. Within the system function (first argument to ode_integrate),
pull out the parameter passed to ode_integrate, assign it to
a local varaible t_delta, then add t_delta to the time argument
in the system.

That parameter t_delta will then be the time offset. I have
no idea whether this will fit well, but it's the only way I know
how to do this.

I'll try to come up with a working example and add a description
to the next manual release:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1709#issuecomment-166691708

If you get it to work before then, please add a comment to the above
issue.

- Bob
